verdict.rationale: Crossmint lets a user give an agent its own signer key bound to a scoped permission set (spend cap, allowed counterparties, time window). That delegation is enforced onchain and revocable. Crossmint also issues scoped, expiring, merchant-locked agent cards with one-time card credentials. These are scoped payment and signing credentials rather than scoped Crossmint platform API keys; the only API-key evidence is client-side keys with URL whitelisting. Missing for 10: least-privilege scoping of Crossmint platform API keys per agent (permission scopes on API keys), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: The user owns a non-custodial wallet and grants the agent scoped permissions (spend limit, counterparties, time window), enforced onchain.
Every delegation is explicit, scoped, and revocable, so the user stays in control.
Save a user's card once and issue scoped, revocable agent cards from it
The merchant is fixed for the lifetime of that order intent, and credential requests inherit the restriction.
